thread.title: Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) Seeks To Capitalize On Facebook, Inc.’s Common Stock (NASDAQ:FB) Anguish

author: Ash Sandifer
title: Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) Seeks To Capitalize On Facebook, Inc.’s Common Stock (NASDAQ:FB) Anguish
text:
Home Technology Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) Seeks To Capitalize On Facebook, Inc.’s Common Stock (NASDAQ:FB) Anguish Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) Seeks To Capitalize On Facebook, Inc.’s Common Stock (NASDAQ:FB) Anguish March 29, 2018 
Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) is searching for ways to take advantage of using customer data in the future after the recent leak of Facebook, Inc.’s Common Stock data to the Cambridge Analytica. In the recent interview on MSNBC TV, Tim Cook CEO of Apple condemned Facebook for failing to update its business model frequently to enhance the privacy of its user data. 
Cook criticized Facebook’s apps stating that the firm made a mistake of factoring in the individual profiles on its platform, which exposes its user data to the unauthorized people. He emphasized that customer privacy is a ‘human right’ and a ‘civil liberty’ for all humans. 
Facebook has been criticized by many people across the world after Observer discovered recently that the personal data of over 50 million users in the US was accessed the electioneering company, Cambridge Analytica. 
Additionally, Cook claimed that for a long time, he has raised the issue on the mass data collection particularly on Google and Facebook but nothing has been done to improve the business model in regard to the regulations on privacy for user data. For decades, Apple has been condemned for not using its user data to enhance its artificial intelligence systems including its virtual assistant Siri. Majority of market analysts have accused Apple for being conservative in the use of data and hence lagging behind other competitors including Google and Amazon. 
Apple’s cautious approach has turned to be an asset as the giant firms including Facebook and Google receive global criticism, which could highly impact on their market shares. Apple is now capitalizing on the blunder and it’s expecting investors to confidently consider the firm’s unique business model that focuses on the privacy of personal information in this age and time. 
Currently, Apple is considering venturing into various sectors including healthcare, where the privacy of user data cannot be compromised. The company plans to launch its own medical clinics for its workforce. Market analysts at UBS have also noted that Apple’s current policy for refuting to share user data for marketing purposes is now a competitive advantage.
